newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp's Reed terms 1996 a "solid" year.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp's Reed terms 1996 a "solid" year.

text.p: Citicorp chairman John Reed, in an annual review for analysts of the company's results, said 1996 was a "solid" year despite a difficult credit environment for bank cards, pricing competition for "big ticket" loans and a squeeze in margins in foreign exchange as currencies in Europe converge.
But overall he said "it was a good solid year in a relatively difficult environment" and the company has been "on track" in the first year of a three-year transition period.
Reed reiterated for the analysts his view that Citicorp will not do acquisitions other than those that specifically support the company's business direction.
He also said one area of interest for a possible acquisition is a business that is focused on serving people who want to build assets for their retirement.
He termed Monday's announcement of a $7.3 billion acquisition of First USA Inc by Banc One Corp a "smart move" for Banc One chairman and chief executive John McCoy.
Referring to the purchase of First USA, a "monoline" company whose primary business is issuing credit cards, Reed said McCoy "bought the best in the industry."
Reed declined to comment on published reports recently which said there had been talks about a combination between American Express Co and Citicorp.

Asked to assess the outlook for the credit card business, which has been experiencing rising chargeoff rates but is profitable, Reed said "I think it is under pressure." He also said the American public has not yet learned to manage family finances in a non-inflationary environment.

Reed noted that there were over one million personal bankruptcies in the U.S. last year. He said there was some reliance on Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to keep the economy in a growth track. "I would hate to see the economy in a downturn," he said.
He said despite tough competition in the bank card business Citicorp has taken a disciplined approach.
Asked if online banking is profitable today, Reed said he believes it is, although Citicorp does not break out figures for that area.
Regarding a squeezing of margins in foreign exchange, Reed said he anticipated "that would continue to be the trend."

With Citicorp booking a substantial part of its revenue and profit overseas, Reed said in response to a question that Hungary, the Czech republic and Poland are doing well, the Middle East is "very solid", the Asia-Pacific region is doing well and Latin America "has come back quite well."
Citicorp's net income in the 1996 fourth quarter was $987 million, up nine percent from a year ago. Earnings per common share rose 15 percent to $1.97.
